purpose: Arformoterol is used to help people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) breathe more easily. It helps keep the airways in your lungs open over a long period of time. It is a maintenance medication, meaning you use it every day to prevent breathing problems, not to treat a sudden attack.
how_it_works: Your airways have tiny muscles around them that can tighten up and make it hard to breathe. Arformoterol works by relaxing those muscles, which allows your airways to open up wider. This makes it easier for air to flow in and out of your lungs, so you feel less short of breath.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include chest pain, back pain, diarrhea, leg cramps, difficulty sleeping, runny or stuffy nose, and a mild rash. Some people may notice a slightly faster or irregular heartbeat. Tell your doctor if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medication should never be used as a rescue inhaler for sudden breathing attacks — always keep a separate fast-acting inhaler for emergencies. Using too much of this type of medication can increase the risk of serious breathing problems or even death in people with asthma. Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid issues, as this medication can affect those conditions. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 15 micrograms (one unit-dose vial) inhaled through a nebulizer machine twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. Each dose takes about 5 to 10 minutes to inhale using the nebulizer.
